instructions.name: accept_contract
docs: Freelancer accepts a funded offer. Does not start the main stream.

instructions.name: add_milestone
docs: Defines one deliverable of a draft milestone contract. The index is
derived on-chain, not supplied by the caller.

accounts.name: employer
docs: Pays rent for the new `WorkUnit`, so must be mutable, and must sign.
`has_one` on the contract below is what ties this signer to *this*
contract's employer.

accounts.name: contract
docs: `Account<Contract>` already proves this is a genuine contract owned by
this program with the right discriminator. Re-deriving the PDA from the
stored identity fields then proves the account sits at its canonical
address, so a cloned copy at some other key cannot be substituted.
`has_one` proves the signer is this contract's employer.

accounts.name: work_unit
docs: The new milestone. Its address is derived from the parent contract and
the parent's current unit count, so the caller has no say in either.

instructions.name: approve_activation
docs: Employer approves activation and establishes main-contract timing.

instructions.name: approve_trial_and_activate
docs: Employer approves submitted trial work and starts the main contract.

instructions.name: approve_work_unit
docs: Employer releases a submitted post-activation work unit. No SPL transfer.

instructions.name: cancel_active_contract
docs: Employer cancels an Active contract and freezes the economic split.
No SPL transfer.

accounts.name: worker
docs: This must match the worker stored in the stream.

instructions.name: claim_employer_refund
docs: Employer claims remaining Phase 7 frozen refundable entitlement.

accounts.name: employer_token_account
docs: Any classic SPL token account of the contract mint owned by the
employer. Not ATA-only.

instructions.name: complete_contract
docs: Permissionless successful completion. No SPL transfer.

accounts.name: caller
docs: Permissionless payer. The result is determined by Clock and state.

instructions.name: create_contract
docs: Creates a funded contract and offers it to the freelancer.

accounts.name: employer
docs: Pays for both new accounts and funds the escrow, so must be mutable and
must sign.

accounts.name: freelancer
docs: No data is read from it, so there is nothing to validate. It is
deliberately not a `SystemAccount`: that would require the freelancer's
wallet to already exist on-chain, excluding anyone who has never held
SOL. The freelancer does not sign here; consent happens in
`accept_contract`.

accounts.name: employer_token_account
docs: Source of the escrow funding. Constrained rather than trusted: without
`token::authority` an attacker could name a token account they do not
own, and without `token::mint` they could fund the escrow with a
worthless token while the contract claims a valuable one.

accounts.name: contract
docs: The contract itself. `init` plus `seeds` means the address is fully
determined by employer, freelancer and `contract_id`, so a forged
contract account cannot be substituted and a duplicate triple is
rejected by the runtime as an already-initialized account.

accounts.name: contract_escrow
docs: The contract's own escrow, derived from the contract's address and owned
by the contract PDA. Three constraints together make a fake escrow
impossible: `seeds` fixes the address, `token::mint` fixes the asset, and
`token::authority` means only this program signing as the contract PDA
can ever move the funds out.

accounts.name: trial_work_unit
docs: Present iff `args.trial_amount > 0`. Initialized at the dedicated
`trial_unit` PDA so it cannot collide with milestone indexes.

accounts.name: fixed_work_unit
docs: Present iff `args.payment_mode == Fixed`. One main deliverable at
`work_unit` index 0, amount = `main_amount`. The freelancer can inspect
it before accepting. Seeds are independent of the trial PDA.

accounts.name: worker
docs: The worker does not need to sign when a stream is created.

instructions.name: decline_contract
docs: Freelancer refuses a funded offer. Escrow is left in place.

instructions.name: finalize_review_timeout
docs: Permissionless auto-release of an expired post-activation review.

accounts.name: caller
docs: Permissionless: the result is determined by clock and unit state, not
by who pays the fee.

instructions.name: finalize_terms
docs: Locks a fully allocated milestone contract's terms and offers it.

accounts.name: contract
docs: Same two checks as `add_milestone`: the account is a real contract at
its canonical PDA, and the signer is its employer.

instructions.name: open_dispute
docs: Employer or freelancer freezes contested economics. No SPL transfer.

accounts.name: party
docs: Employer or freelancer. Identity is checked against stored keys.

instructions.name: reject_activation
docs: Employer declines to activate after the trial stage. Escrow is left in place.

accounts.name: trial_work_unit
docs: Required when a trial is configured; omitted otherwise.

instructions.name: release_stream_accrual
docs: Materialize currently accrued streaming earnings into released accounting.
Permissionless and deterministic. No SPL transfer.

accounts.name: caller
docs: Permissionless: the result does not depend on who pays the fee.

instructions.name: request_revision
docs: Employer requests a bounded resubmission of post-activation work.

instructions.name: request_trial_revision
docs: Employer requests a bounded trial revision.

instructions.name: resolve_dispute
docs: Per-contract resolver allocates the contested remainder. No SPL transfer.

instructions.name: submit_trial_work
docs: Freelancer submits paid trial work. Does not release funds or activate.

instructions.name: submit_work_unit
docs: Freelancer submits post-activation Milestone or Fixed work.

instructions.name: withdraw_freelancer
docs: Freelancer withdraws all currently available released/settled entitlement.

accounts.name: contract_escrow
docs: Canonical escrow for this Contract. Seeds bind it to `contract`; mint
and authority bind it to the funded asset and the Contract PDA.

accounts.name: freelancer_token_account
docs: Any classic SPL token account of the contract mint owned by the
freelancer. Not ATA-only.

types.name: ActivationRejected
docs: The employer reviewed the trial stage and declined to activate.

fields.name: version
docs: On-chain layout version, for forward migration.

fields.name: employer
docs: The client funding the work.

fields.name: freelancer
docs: The worker performing it.

fields.name: token_mint
docs: SPL mint of the escrowed token. Classic SPL Token only.

fields.name: contract_id
docs: Employer-scoped identifier; part of the PDA seeds.

fields.name: total_amount
docs: Amount funded into escrow at creation. Immutable.

fields.name: trial_amount
docs: Reserved pre-activation trial compensation, included in `total_amount`.
Zero means no trial is configured. Not a lifecycle predicate: whether a
trial WorkUnit exists is answered by this being positive *and* the
`trial_unit` PDA being initialized.

fields.name: main_amount
docs: Main-contract economic base: `total_amount - trial_amount`. Future
streaming, fixed and milestone settlement uses this, never the trial
reservation. Equals `total_amount` when there is no trial.

fields.name: allocated_amount
docs: Sum of defined milestone work unit amounts. Milestone/Fixed only.
At finalize this must equal `main_amount`, not `total_amount`.

fields.name: released_amount
docs: Freelancer entitlement unlocked by approval or review timeout.

fields.name: withdrawn_amount
docs: Portion of `released_amount` already transferred out.

fields.name: refunded_amount
docs: Unreleased funds already returned to the employer.

fields.name: stream_released_amount
docs: Streaming main-work already materialized into `released_amount`.
Independent of any trial credit, so
`released_amount` conceptually equals `trial_released + stream_released_amount`
on an Active streaming contract. Never inferred from `released_amount`.

fields.name: freelancer_settlement_amount
docs: Frozen freelancer entitlement after cancellation, dispute resolution,
or successful completion. Zero until those terminal settlements.
Equals `released_amount` at freeze.

fields.name: employer_refundable_amount
docs: Frozen employer refundable entitlement after cancellation, dispute
resolution, or successful completion. Zero until settlement. Not tokens
transferred: that is `refunded_amount`.

fields.name: resolver
docs: Per-contract arbitrator. Bound at creation; never the employer,
freelancer, or default. Immutable after `create_contract`.

fields.name: contested_amount
docs: Unresolved remainder at dispute open:
`total_amount - released_amount - refunded_amount` after any stream freeze.

fields.name: disputed_at
docs: Instant `open_dispute` (or submitted-trial reject) froze economics.

fields.name: acceptance_deadline
docs: Latest instant at which the freelancer may accept.

fields.name: scheduled_start_time
docs: Agreed start instant. Only read when `start_mode == Scheduled`.

fields.name: duration_seconds
docs: Streaming length. Needed to resolve `end_time` at activation, since
under `OnActivation` the start instant is unknown at creation.

fields.name: checkpoint_interval
docs: Streaming checkpoint period length. Only read when the payment mode
uses checkpoints.

fields.name: review_duration
docs: Length of both the employer review window and the freelancer
resubmission window.

fields.name: activation_review_duration
docs: How long the employer has, after freelancer acceptance, to approve or
reject activation. Frozen at creation. The deadline is derived as
`accepted_at + activation_review_duration` once the freelancer accepts.

fields.name: max_revisions
docs: Agreed cap on revision cycles per work unit. Together with
`review_duration` this bounds worst-case withholding.

fields.name: start_time
docs: Resolved at employer activation from `start_mode`.

fields.name: end_time
docs: Resolved at employer activation as `start_time + duration_seconds`.

fields.name: last_period_end
docs: Streaming checkpoint cursor: the end of the most recently created
period. Guarantees periods are contiguous and non-overlapping.

fields.name: terminated_at
docs: Instant the contract was cancelled or completed; anchors the
post-termination grace window.

fields.name: work_unit_count
docs: Next work unit index to allocate.

fields.name: open_review_count
docs: Units currently in a non-terminal reviewable state. A non-zero value
blocks employer cancellation.

fields.name: last_milestone_due_offset
docs: Due offset of the most recently defined milestone, in seconds after
start. Zero until the first milestone exists. Used so `add_milestone`
can enforce strictly increasing offsets without iterating children.

fields.name: metadata_hash
docs: Hash of the canonical off-chain record, making it tamper-evident.

fields.name: reserved
docs: Upgrade headroom. Adding a field means shrinking this, which leaves
account size and every client offset unchanged.
Started at 128 bytes; `voided_unit_count` (4),
`last_milestone_due_offset` (8), `activation_review_duration` (8),
`trial_amount` (8), `main_amount` (8), `stream_released_amount` (8),
`freelancer_settlement_amount` (8) and `employer_refundable_amount` (8)
were taken from it.
Phase 7 layout: two u64 settlement fields after `stream_released_amount`;
reserved 84 → 68. Phase 9 consumed 49 more bytes for `resolver` (32),
`contested_amount` (8), `disputed_at` (8) and `dispute_initiator` (1);
reserved 68 → 19. `INIT_SPACE` remains 621.

fields.name: metadata_uri
docs: Bounded pointer to the off-chain record.

types.name: ContractAccepted
docs: The freelancer accepted a funded offer. The main stream has not started.

types.name: ContractActivated
docs: The employer approved activation. Main-contract timing is now established.

types.name: ContractCancellationSettled
docs: An Active contract was cancelled and its economic split was frozen.
No SPL transfer.

types.name: ContractCompleted
docs: Successful completion froze the agreed economic end. No SPL transfer.

types.name: ContractCreated
docs: A contract was created and fully funded into escrow.
`status` is included because it is the one field an indexer cannot infer:
it distinguishes a contract that is immediately offerable
(`PendingAcceptance`) from a milestone contract still awaiting its
allocation (`Draft`).

types.name: ContractDeclined
docs: The freelancer refused a funded offer.

types.name: ContractStatus
docs: Authoritative contract lifecycle state.
Borsh unit-enum discriminants, old → new (V2 was never deployed):
| variant                  | old | new |
| Draft                    | 0   | 0   |
| PendingAcceptance        | 1   | 1   |
| PendingEmployerApproval  | —   | 2   |
| Active                   | 2   | 3   |
| Completed                | 3   | 4   |
| Declined                 | 4   | 5   |
| Expired                  | 5   | 6   |
| Cancelled                | 6   | 7   |
| ActivationRejected       | —   | 8   |
| Disputed                 | —   | 9   |
| Resolved                 | —   | 10  |
`PendingEmployerApproval` is the employer-approval gate: the freelancer has
accepted, the main stream has not started. `ActivationRejected` is the
employer's "no" at that gate, distinct from `Declined` (the freelancer
refused the offer). Events distinguish the two paths for indexers; status
distinguishes them for on-chain logic.

types.name: CreateContractArgs
docs: Caller-supplied terms.
Grouped into a struct rather than a dozen positional parameters so that
adding a term in a later phase cannot silently shift an existing argument's
meaning at the call site.
Every field here is a *term*. No lifecycle or accounting field is accepted
from the caller: `status`, all five money counters, all unit counters, every
lifecycle timestamp and both bumps are derived by the handler below.

fields.name: contract_id
docs: Employer-scoped identifier. Part of the PDA seeds, so reusing one for
the same freelancer is rejected by the runtime, not by a check here.

fields.name: total_amount
docs: Funded in full during this instruction.

fields.name: acceptance_deadline
docs: Latest instant the freelancer may accept.

fields.name: scheduled_start_time
docs: Only meaningful when `start_mode == Scheduled`; normalized away
otherwise. See `resolve`.

fields.name: duration_seconds
docs: Length of the contract term, in seconds.

fields.name: checkpoint_interval
docs: Only meaningful when `payment_mode == Streaming`; normalized away
otherwise. See `resolve`.

fields.name: review_duration
docs: Employer review window, and equally the freelancer's resubmission
window.

fields.name: activation_review_duration
docs: How long the employer has after freelancer acceptance to approve
activation. Does not start the stream by itself.

fields.name: trial_amount
docs: Paid pre-activation trial reservation, included in `total_amount`.
Zero means no trial. Must be strictly less than `total_amount` so the
main contract retains a positive economic base.

fields.name: resolver
docs: Per-contract dispute resolver. Must differ from employer, freelancer,
and the default pubkey. Frozen at creation.

fields.name: metadata_uri
docs: Bounded reference to the off-chain contract record.

fields.name: metadata_hash
docs: Hash of that record, making it tamper-evident.

types.name: DisputeOpened
docs: A party froze the contract into Disputed. No SPL transfer.

types.name: DisputeParty
docs: Who opened an on-chain dispute. `None` until `open_dispute` / trial reject.

types.name: DisputeResolved
docs: The contract resolver allocated the contested remainder. No SPL transfer.

types.name: EmployerRefundClaimed
docs: SPL tokens left escrow back to the employer. Real token movement.

types.name: FreelancerWithdrawal
docs: SPL tokens left escrow for the freelancer. Real token movement.

types.name: MilestoneAdded
docs: One milestone was defined on a draft contract.
`allocated_amount` is the running total after this milestone, so an indexer
can tell how much of the escrow is still unallocated without re-reading the
contract. Titles and specifications are not here: they live in the
contract's off-chain record.

types.name: PaymentMode
docs: How compensation is structured and released.
The three modes are mutually exclusive: a streaming contract never has
milestones, and a milestone/fixed contract never has checkpoints. That
exclusivity is what lets a single `WorkUnit` type and a single index space
serve all three.

types.name: ReleaseTrigger
docs: Why a work unit's amount became released.
A typed "not yet" variant rather than a sentinel value; only meaningful
once `WorkUnitStatus::Released`.

types.name: StartMode
docs: When the main earning clock starts.
Discriminants are stable: `OnActivation` is 0, `Scheduled` is 1. This was
previously named `OnAcceptance`; it was renamed before V2 deployment because
freelancer acceptance no longer starts the stream.

types.name: StreamAccrualReleased
docs: Time-based streaming earnings were materialized into released accounting.
No SPL transfer.

types.name: TermsFinalized
docs: A milestone contract's terms became immutable and the contract is now
offered to the freelancer.

types.name: TrialApproved
docs: The employer approved the trial. Compensation is released, not withdrawn.

types.name: TrialConfigured
docs: A paid trial was configured at contract creation.

types.name: TrialRejected
docs: The employer rejected submitted trial work. No tokens moved.

types.name: TrialRevisionRequested
docs: The employer requested a trial revision.

types.name: TrialSubmitted
docs: The freelancer submitted (or resubmitted) trial work.

fields.name: version
docs: On-chain layout version, for forward migration.

fields.name: contract
docs: Parent contract. Stored in addition to being a PDA seed: the seed
constraint proves derivation and this field enables a `has_one` check,
so cross-contract substitution is caught two independent ways.

fields.name: index
docs: Zero-based index within the parent contract, and part of the PDA seeds,
which makes a duplicate unit unrepresentable.

fields.name: amount
docs: Amount credited to `Contract::released_amount` when this unit is
released. Immutable once submitted.

fields.name: period_start
docs: Inclusive start of the streaming period. `Checkpoint` only.

fields.name: period_end
docs: Exclusive end of the streaming period. `Checkpoint` only.

fields.name: due_offset_seconds
docs: Seconds after `Contract::start_time` when this deliverable is due.
`Milestone` / `Fixed` only. Always a duration, never a calendar
timestamp, so the same field is valid under both `OnActivation` and
`Scheduled`. Absolute due time is `start_time + due_offset_seconds`
once the contract has actually started.

fields.name: submitted_at
docs: When the current submission was made.

fields.name: action_deadline
docs: Deadline for whichever party must act next, determined by `status`:
- `Submitted`: the employer's review deadline. Once it passes, review
timeout finalization may release the amount.
- `Revising`: the freelancer's resubmission deadline. Once it passes,
the employer may void the stale unit, which is what stops an absent
freelancer from blocking cancellation forever.
- any other status: not read, and never used as a lifecycle predicate.

fields.name: approved_at
docs: When the employer signed an approval.

fields.name: released_at
docs: When the amount was credited to the contract's released total.

fields.name: revision_count
docs: Revision cycles consumed, bounded by `Contract::max_revisions`.

fields.name: release_trigger
docs: Why the unit was released. Only meaningful once `status == Released`.

fields.name: submission_hash
docs: Hash of the off-chain deliverable, making it tamper-evident.

fields.name: reserved
docs: Upgrade headroom; see `Contract::reserved`.

fields.name: submission_uri
docs: Bounded pointer to the off-chain deliverable. Work files themselves are
never stored on-chain.

types.name: WorkUnitApproved
docs: The employer approved a submitted work unit. Compensation is released, not withdrawn.

types.name: WorkUnitKind
docs: Which flavour of work unit this account represents.
Checkpoints are created by the freelancer at submission time with an amount
derived from the agreed vesting formula. Milestones are created by the
employer before acceptance with a negotiated amount.

types.name: WorkUnitReviewTimedOut
docs: Review timed out and the submitted unit was auto-released. No SPL transfer.

types.name: WorkUnitRevisionRequested
docs: The employer requested a bounded resubmission of post-activation work.

types.name: WorkUnitStatus
docs: Authoritative work unit lifecycle state.

types.name: WorkUnitSubmitted
docs: The freelancer submitted (or resubmitted) post-activation work.
